name: item-context
body:
Every slide layout and every section template, at any nesting depth, is additionally given a reserved `item` context describing the current instance's place among its siblings: `index` (0-based), `number` (1-based), `count` (the number of siblings in the same parent section), `first` and `last` (booleans), `section` (the section name) and `template` (the resolved template), and `parent` (the parent instance's fields, or nil at the top level). At slide level `item` is nil or absent — a slide has no siblings. `item` is a reserved top-level name: neither a field nor a section may be named `item`, and neither may be named `raw` or `data` (requirements.constraint.reserved-template-names). Exposing `item` adds no layout helper: the helper set is `media`, `section`, `dict` and `list` (template-language). A section invoked by the `section` helper receives a one-item descriptor: `section` and `template` are the target name, `index` 0, `number` 1, `count` 1, `first` and `last` true, and `parent` is the calling instance's fields (nil when the call is made from a slide layout) — see section-helper, section-template-context.

AC: a layout or section template can read `{{.item.number}}`, `{{.item.count}}`, `{{.item.first}}`, `{{.item.last}}`, `{{.item.section}}`, `{{.item.template}}` and `{{.item.parent.<field>}}`; the values reflect the instance's position among its siblings (index 0-based, number 1-based); a slide layout sees `item` nil/absent; a `section`-helper invocation sees the one-item descriptor; loading a template that declares a field or section named `item` (or `raw`/`data`) is a templates error.
